detail.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm, softmax MoE routing uses AITER's legacy `topkGatingSoftmax` launcher. This routes `FusedTopKRouter` and the fused-shared-expert router (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`) through `aiter.ops.topk.topk_gating` instead, which keeps selected-mass renormalization in-kernel (ROCm/aiter#4460), has the E=512 `prefill_n` dispatch (ROCm/aiter#5334), and with ROCm/aiter#6306 scores the shared-expert columns with sigmoid in the same launch. `dispatch_topk_softmax_func` decides per launch between `topk_gating` and the legacy `topk_softmax`. This PR makes the selection the default on CDNA3 and CDNA4 (gfx942, gfx950); every other architecture keeps the legacy launcher. gfx950 is the main sweep; gfx942 (MI300-class) was verified more lightly (see the gfx942 section). The blast radius is implicitly limited to Qwens, because based on my search other models won't use the `topk_gating`.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for `topk_gating` and `aiter topk softmax`; no other PR routes softmax top-k through `topk_gating`. #57246 fixes the eager `torch.topk` fallback in `fused_topk_bias`, and #55147 fixes the width of the `topk_ids` buffer AITER's kernels write; neither changes which AITER launcher is used.

## Claims

- On the same nightly, with only this PR and ROCm/aiter#6306 added, `topk_gating` is **+0.7% to +1.5% output-throughput geomean per cell** for Flash-Next (E=512, top-10, one shared expert) at TP2 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` 1 and 0, at three `max-num-batched-tokens` (2048, 4096, 8192), and **+1.3% to +1.9%** for Qwen3-30B-A3B (E=128, top-8) at TP1 in two passes per cell, over the four rows that repeat. Single-stream decode (1k/1k, concurrency 1) is the largest effect: +2.0% to +4.4% in every cell.
- Kernel: for E=512 / top-10 with one shared expert, `topk_gating` is 37–47% faster than `topk_softmax(..., "sigmoid")` at T ≤ 1024 and level at T = 2048–4096 (AITER op test, table below).
- No directional accuracy change: GSM8K on all 9 cells, paired, 134 problems fixed and 126 broken in total (net +8 of 11,871), no cell below p = 0.12. The six cells of the Qwen3-30B rerun are also consistent with noise (no cell below p = 0.39).
- gfx942 (MI300-class): the kernel passes AITER's op test and the vLLM unit tests there with zero routing mismatches, is neutral to slightly positive end to end (+2.0% and +0.45% output-throughput geomean on Qwen3-30B at mbt 4096 and 2048; +1.4% to +4.7% on three Flash-Next-FP8 TP2 rows), and GSM8K is unchanged (no cell below p = 0.16). This is a lighter check than the gfx950 sweep; details below.
- Which launches change: on CDNA3 and CDNA4 (gfx942, gfx950), contiguous gating rows with T ≤ 4096 tokens, and shared experts only with sigmoid scoring and 1, 2, 4 or 8 shared experts. Everything else, and every other GPU architecture, keeps `topk_softmax`. **There is no env var to turn it on/off.**

## Validation

**Unit tests.** On one MI355X, in the candidate image (below):

```bash
pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py tests/model_executor/test_enabled_custom_ops.py -k topk
# 74 passed, 19 deselected   (at b4c61b0e0)
pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py tests/model_executor/test_enabled_custom_ops.py
# 93 passed
```

On gfx942 (MI300-class), on the nightly base with this PR's net diff and the gate change applied: 35 passed in `test_enabled_custom_ops.py -k topk` and 39 in `test_rocm_aiter_topk.py`.

`tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py` checks the shared-expert suffix against a torch reference; `test_topk_softmax_dispatch_aiter_topk_gating` pins which launcher each launch shape takes, on the enabled architectures and (monkeypatched) on another one: shared-expert sigmoid with 1/2/4/8 shared experts, an unsupported count, wrong or missing shared scoring, mismatched row strides, a narrow weights buffer, non-contiguous rows, T = 4096 versus 4097, and the kill switch (each launch shape on gfx950 and elsewhere).

**Kernel evidence.** `op_tests/test_moe_topk_gating.py` from ROCm/aiter#6306, MI355X, E=512, top-10, bf16, renorm, one shared expert. Mean kernel time per call, one run, lower is better. Every case has 0 routing mismatches against a torch reference.

| T | `topk_gating` (µs) | legacy `topk_softmax` (µs) | Δ |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 5.56 | 9.76 | −43% |
| 16 | 5.87 | 10.51 | −44% |
| 64 | 5.86 | 10.86 | −46% |
| 256 | 6.05 | 11.42 | −47% |
| 1024 | 6.56 | 10.42 | −37% |
| 2048 | 10.66 | 10.60 | +0.5% |
| 4096 | 12.84 | 13.14 | −2.3% |

Above T = 1024 the kernel runs its shared-memory fallback, which is level with the legacy launcher; above T = 4096 vLLM keeps the legacy launcher (`_AITER_TOPK_GATING_MAX_TOKENS`), where an earlier measurement had `topk_gating` losing at 8K-token prefill chunks.

**End to end.** MI355X (gfx950). Both arms are the same image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93`; the candidate adds only this PR's vLLM diff. Server flags in both arms: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `--max-num-seqs 256`, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, `--trust-remote-code`, thinking off, and `--max-num-batched-tokens` as in the column. It was verified that every candidate server loaded `module_moe_topk`; no control server did. Router `T` is the decode concurrency in decode rows and `min(mbt, prompt)` per prefill chunk, so prefill chunks at mbt 8192 take the legacy launcher in both arms.

Flash-Next is `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4` at TP2 (`--max-model-len 262144 --reasoning-parser qwen3`). Qwen3-30B-A3B is `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` (bf16) at TP1.

Reading the table:

- **Gain at small `T`, flat at large `T`.** Concurrency 1 gains +2.0% to +4.4% in every cell, while the 8k and 16k rows sit at about +0.5% to +1%: their steps are dominated by prefill chunks of 2048 tokens or more, where the kernel is level with the legacy launcher (and above 4096 the legacy launcher runs in both arms). That matches the kernel table, where the saving is about 4–5 µs per layer launch at small `T` and nothing at T ≥ 2048.
- **FSE does not change the picture.** With FSE=1 the candidate also fuses the sigmoid shared-expert scoring (the suffix from #6306); with FSE=0 `topk_gating` runs without it. The cell geomeans are +1.1% to +1.5% and +0.7% to +1.2%.
- **TTFT.** Prefill is where `topk_gating` helps least, so the TTFT geomean is flat: −1.5% to +0.0% across the six Flash-Next cells and −2.3% to +0.5% across the Qwen3-30B passes, which is the size of the run-to-run noise.

| Flash-Next FSE=0, mbt 8192 | 0.9629 → 0.9674 | 14 / 8 | 0.286 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, mbt 2048 | 0.9045 → 0.9030 | 16 / 18 | 0.864 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, mbt 4096 | 0.9067 → 0.9075 | 17 / 16 | 1.000 |

The flexible-extract scores move the same way. The Qwen3-30B rows above are from the first sweep. The rerun's six cells (two passes at each mbt) are also consistent with noise: strict-match 0.9014–0.9083 on both arms, exact McNemar p between 0.39 and 1.0.

**gfx942 (MI300-class).** This is a verification, not a repeat of the full gfx950 sweep. Node: 8x MI300-class (gfx942), image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93` (AITER 0.1.24.post1). Candidate: this PR with the gfx942 gate plus ROCm/aiter#6306 (`15f14c767`) with `module_moe_topk` rebuilt for gfx942; the candidate server loads `module_moe_topk`, the control does not.

*Kernel.* `op_tests/test_moe_topk_gating.py` passes on gfx942: NaN/Inf, exact ties, fake-EPLB balance and the shared-expert cases, all error columns 0 (max weight error at most 3e-8). Fused `topk_gating` time for E=512, top-10, bf16, one shared expert:

The per-T legacy times from that run were not kept, so those percentages are not backed by a table here. The shape matches gfx950, where T = 2048 and 4096 are level.

```bash
# candidate: the same image with this PR and ROCm/aiter#6306 applied

  --max-model-len 262144 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --trust-remote-code \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'

python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --dataset-name random --request-rate inf \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 128 --warmup-requests 32 --seed 302

  --model_args model=amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,timeout=1200,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,max_gen_toks=2048 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template --batch_size 32 --seed 4321 --log_samples

pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py tests/model_executor/test_enabled_custom_ops.py -k topk
```

The other rows use `--random-input-len/--random-output-len/--max-concurrency/--num-prompts/--warmup-requests/--seed` of 1024/1024/1/8/1/301, 1024/1024/128/256/128/303, 8192/128/8/32/8/304, 8192/1024/32/64/32/305 and 16384/128/2/8/2/306.

## Details

**What runs before and after.** Before, every softmax top-k on ROCm with AITER (`FusedTopKRouter`, and the fused-shared-expert router) ran `topk_softmax`, AITER's legacy launcher. After, `dispatch_topk_softmax_func` takes the launch's tensors and shared-expert arguments and returns `rocm_aiter_ops.topk_gating` on CDNA3 and CDNA4 (gfx942, gfx950) when `_aiter_topk_gating_supported` accepts the launch, and `topk_softmax` otherwise (including on every other architecture). `_aiter_topk_gating_supported` accepts contiguous gating rows with at most 4096 tokens; with shared experts it also needs sigmoid scoring, 1, 2, 4 or 8 of them, `topk_weights` and `topk_indices` sharing a row stride, and `topk_weights` wide enough for the shared columns. The shared-expert ids stay as the caller prefilled them, as with the legacy launcher. `_rocm_aiter_topk_gating_impl` is a plain call into `aiter.ops.topk.topk_gating`; the router runs inside the opaque `moe_forward` custom op, so nothing here changes graph capture.

**Why the 4096-token cap.** At E=512 / top-10 the kernel is level with the legacy launcher at T = 2048 and 4096 and was slower at 8K-token prefill chunks in an earlier measurement, so above 4096 the legacy launcher keeps serving. The cap is a named constant in the router, not a magic number.

**Why no env var.** The sweep shows a small positive effect at every shape tested on gfx950 and no reproducible loss, so there is nothing to opt into, and the path is the default under the existing AITER enablement (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE`) on gfx942 and gfx950. gfx942 was verified more lightly than gfx950 (see the gfx942 section); the gate is one line (`is_topk_gating_enabled`), so another architecture can be added the same way once it is measured.
